To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) incentive salience is an additional motivational component of reward that can decouple cue-triggering of motivation from all previous memories of reward value, 2) incentive salience can generate irrationally strong motivational urges, and 3) these motivational urges are controlled by neurobiological state variables that are independent of learning.

incentive salience is a separate computational component of reward function that is generated by the ventral tegmental area (VTA), nucleus accumbens (NAc) and prefrontal cortex, and that neurobiological state can independently control incentive salience.

incentive salience takes as inputs both Pavlovian learning (which determines how much reward value is predicted from a cue) and neurobiological state (which determines how motivated one is to act on that predicted reward value), and incentive salience generates a motivational urge that is independent of the predicted value of the reward, and that can be either stronger or weaker than the value prediction, depending on the state factors that are present.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain computes the motivational value of rewards.
how incentive salience and prediction error interact in reward circuitry.
the neurobiology of motivation and how it can depart from learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the motivational component of reward is not a simple consequence of learning and memory.
incentive salience is a distinct computational process that can be generated in parallel to learning and that can be controlled by neurobiological state changes.

incentive salience is not a simple consequence of prediction error or learning, but is a complex and independent process of its own that takes prediction error and neurobiological state as two separate inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

incentive salience is a distinct neurobiological process that takes as inputs the learned value of a reward cue and a state of the organism, and produces an output of motivation to approach the associated reward.

incentive salience is a neurocomputational mechanism for the motivational component of reward that is distinct from learning and memory, and that incentive salience has important functions in the control of behavior.
incentive salience is a neurobiologically controlled computation that is distinct from prediction error, and is a critical factor in reward motivation and its disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that

incentive salience can produce motivational urges that are not predicted by learning, and these motivational urges are generated by a separate computation in the brain that takes Pavlovian memory as one input, and neurobiological state as another important input.
the incentive salience computation of reward motivation is not the same as learning, and is controlled in addition by neurobiological state.
incentive salience is not a simple function of learning.
